Curved TV screens are reported to improve presence and visual comfort in a peer-reviewed study under specific viewing distances and screen sizes, with 18% higher visual presence for 2D and 9% for 3D at 2 m on a 45" curved model versus a flat one [d1]. However, technical analysis from LG Display contends that curved screens only deliver optimal quality for a single viewer at the exact center and introduce line distortions, undermining broader benefits [d8]. Popular and marketing sources emphasize immersion, reduced glare, and aesthetic appeal as advantages of curved designs [d2, d3, d5, d6, d7], while reviewer commentary highlights a narrow “sweet spot” and limited real-world benefits compared with flat screens [d4].

Given these conflicting findings and the lack of consensus on general superiority, there is no definitive evidence that curved TV screens are universally better for viewing.
